formulations.label: Sublingual tablets
formulations.note: Placed under the tongue. Contains lactose. Discard 8 weeks after first opening the bottle.

src.q: Each tablet contains 500 micrograms Glyceryl Trinitrate.
Excipients with known effect: Also contains lactose
Discard 8 weeks after first opening.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Short-acting vasodilator: relief of angina pectoris, prophylaxis of angina pectoris, and relief of acute spontaneous coronary artery spasm.

src.q: As a short-acting vasodilator Relief of angina pectoris Prophylaxis of angina pectoris Relief of acute spontaneous coronary artery spasm

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction or brand-specific prescribing statement in the two UK SPCs used (MHRA products); no MHRA Drug Safety Update or SPS advice found for glyceryl trinitrate tablets. No GTN sublingual tablet SmPC is listed on emc.

items.t: Acute attack: one tablet (0.5 mg) under the tongue when angina starts; may repeat every 5 minutes up to a total of three doses. If symptoms persist after three doses, seek prompt medical attention. Rest sitting down (risk of postural hypotension).

src.q: When angina starts, 0.5 mg glyceryl trinitrate (one tablet) should be taken and if symptoms do not resolve, may be repeated at five minute intervals for a total of three doses.
If symptoms have not resolved after a total of three doses, the patient should seek prompt medical attention.
The patient should preferably rest in the sitting position because of the risk of symptomatic postural hypotension.

items.t: Prophylaxis: one tablet (0.5 mg) before activity likely to bring on angina.

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate, 0.5 mg (one tablet), may be used prior to activity which is likely to precipitate angina pectoris.

items.t: Elderly: hypotension and syncope are a particular problem; advise sitting down when taking it.

src.q: Hypotension and syncope can be a particular problem with use of nitrates in the elderly.
Patients should be advised to sit down whenever possible when taking sublingual glyceryl trinitrate.

items.t: No data on use in children; no child dose given.

src.q: Children No data are available on the use of glyceryl trinitrate in children.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to glyceryl trinitrate, other nitro compounds or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance, to other nitro compounds or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Patients taking PDE5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil).

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate is contraindicated in patients taking phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil)

items.t: Angina caused by hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (may worsen outflow obstruction); possible raised intracranial pressure (e.g. cerebral haemorrhage, head trauma); marked anaemia; closed-angle glaucoma.

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate is contraindicated in angina caused by hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy as it may exaggerate outflow obstruction.
Glyceryl trinitrate should not be used in patients with possible increased intracranial pressure (e.g. cerebral haemorrhage or head trauma). - Marked anaemia - Closed angle glaucoma

items.t: Use with caution where adequate preload is needed for cardiac output: acute circulatory shock (hypovolaemic, or cardiogenic with inadequate filling pressure), severe mitral stenosis, pericardial tamponade, constrictive pericarditis, orthostatic dysfunction.

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate should be used with caution in patients in whom adequate preload is important for maintaining cardiac output (e.g. acute circulatory shock including hypovolemic shock or cardiogenic shock with inadequate diastolic filling pressures, severe mitral stenosis

items.t: Use with caution in severe hypotension (systolic below 90 mmHg) and in cerebrovascular disease (hypotension may precipitate symptoms).

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate should be used with caution in patients with severe hypotension (systolic blood pressure below 90 mm Hg)
Glyceryl trinitrate should be used with caution in patients with cerebrovascular disease since symptoms may be precipitated by hypotension.

items.t: May worsen hypoxaemia in lung disease or cor pulmonale. Hypotension with bradycardia may occur after myocardial infarction. Be cautious in angina with moderate to severe valvular aortic stenosis.

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate may worsen hypoxaemia in patients with lung disease or cor pulmonale.
Arterial hypotension with bradycardia may occur in patients with myocardial infarction
it seems prudent to be cautious in treating ambulant patients with the combination of angina and moderate to severe valvular aortic stenosis

items.t: Caution in severe hepatic or renal impairment, hypothyroidism, hypoxaemia, hypothermia, recent myocardial infarction and malnutrition.

src.q: Caution is necessary in patients with severe hepatic or renal impairment, hypothyroidism, hypoxaemia, hypothermia or a recent history of myocardial infaraction and malnutrition.

items.t: Contains lactose: patients with hereditary galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose- galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil): potentiate the hypotensive effect. Contraindicated.

src.q: have been shown to potentiate the hypotensive effects of nitrates, and coadministration with glyceryl trinitrate is therefore contraindicated

items.t: Other hypotensive agents (vasodilators, antihypertensives, beta-blockers, calcium-channel blockers, neuroleptics, tricyclic antidepressants, sapropterin) may increase the hypotensive effect; alcohol may increase hypotension and syncope.

src.q: Treatment with other agents with hypotensive effects (e.g. vasodilators, antihypertensives, beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers and neuroleptics, tricyclic antidepressants and sapropterin) may potentiate the hypotensive effect of glyceryl trinitrate.
the risk of hypotension and syncope with use of glyceryl trinitrate may be enhanced by alcohol

items.t: Medicines that cause dry mouth (anticholinergics, antimuscarinics, tricyclic antidepressants) may reduce the effect of sublingual nitrates.

src.q: There is a potential for drugs that cause dry mouth (eg anticholinergic, antimuscarinics, tricyclic antidepressants) to reduce the effectiveness of sublingual nitrates.

items.t: Long-acting nitrates: consider the possibility of tolerance to glyceryl trinitrate.

src.q: The possibility of tolerance to the effects of glyceryl trinitrate should be considered when used in conjunction with long-acting nitrate preparations.

items.t: Heparin: systemic nitrates may interfere with its anticoagulant effect; monitor anticoagulation early and often. Also: N-acetylcysteine (more vasodilatation), sublingual apomorphine (more hypotension), ergot alkaloids (oppose effect; higher dihydroergotamine exposure).

src.q: Early and frequent monitoring of anticoagulation is recommended when systemic nitrates and heparin are used in combination.
N-acetylcysteine may potentiate the vasodilator effects of glyceryl trinitrate.
An enhanced hypotensive effect with sublingual apomorphine may occur
Ergot alkaloids may oppose the coronary vasodilatation of nitrates.

items.t: Caution in severe renal impairment. No numeric threshold or dose adjustment given.

src.q: Caution is necessary in patients with severe hepatic or renal impairment

items.t: Caution in severe hepatic impairment. No dose adjustment given.

src.q: Caution is necessary in patients with severe hepatic or renal impairment

items.t: Animal studies show no harm, but human relevance is unknown. Consider use only if the expected benefit to the mother is greater than any possible risk to the fetus. No BUMPS leaflet for nitrates was found.

src.q: The administration of glyceryl trinitrate during pregnancy should only be considered if the expected benefit to the mother is greater than any possible risk to the foetus.

items.t: Not known whether it passes into milk; a risk to the infant cannot be excluded. Decide whether to stop breastfeeding or stop treatment, weighing benefits. No SPS breastfeeding page for oral nitrates was found.

src.q: It is unknown if glyceryl trinitrate or its metabolites are excreted in human milk. A risk to the suckling child cannot be excluded.
A decision must be made whether to discontinue/abstain from breast-feeding or to discontinue/abstain from glyceryl trinitrate therapy

items.t: Animal studies showed no harmful effects on fertility; relevance to humans unknown.

src.q: Fertility Animal studies did not indicate harmful effects with respect to fertility.

items.t: Headache and dizziness (can persist after the pain has gone; removing the tablet before it fully dissolves can reduce this); postural hypotension, especially at the start of treatment or after a dose increase; local burning or tingling under the tongue. The frequency table in the SPC PDF text could not be read reliably, so frequencies are not given here.

src.q: Particularly upon initiation of therapy and following an increase in dose.
because of the risk of symptomatic postural hypotension
Headache and dizziness, persisting after relief of angina may be minimised by removing the glyceryl trinitrate tablet before it has completely dissolved.
A local burning or tingling sensation may occur.

items.t: Hypotension from glyceryl trinitrate may cause cerebral ischaemia; circulatory collapse and syncope are listed.

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate-induced hypotension may cause cerebral ischaemia.

items.t: Large doses may cause vomiting, cyanosis, restlessness, methaemoglobinaemia and impaired breathing. If angina is not relieved after three doses, seek prompt medical attention.

src.q: Large dose of glyceryl trinitrate may cause vomiting, cyanosis, restlessness, methaemoglobinaemia and impairment of respiration.
If angina symptoms have not resolved after a total of three doses, the patient should be instructed to seek prompt medical attention

monitoring.note: No laboratory or routine monitoring stated in the two UK SPCs used; no SPS monitoring page found for nitrates.

items.t: Place under the tongue and keep in the mouth until dissolved or discarded. A local burning or tingling sensation may occur.

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate must be placed under the tongue (administered sublingually) and retained in the mouth until dissolved or discarded.

items.t: Keep in the original glass bottle with the cap tightly closed, below 25°C and protected from light; do not add cotton wool or other tablets. Discard 8 weeks after first opening.

src.q: Keep them in this. After use reclose the bottle cap tightly. Do not put cotton wool, other drugs, or anything else in the bottle with the tablets.
If you do not use the tablets within 8 weeks of first opening the bottle, obtain a fresh supply and return the old tablets to your pharmacist.

items.t: Sit down when taking a tablet. Take one tablet at the start of an attack; repeat every 5 minutes up to three tablets. If pain is not relieved after three tablets, get urgent medical help.

src.q: If symptoms have not resolved after a total of three doses, the patient should seek prompt medical attention.
Patients should be advised to sit down whenever possible when taking sublingual glyceryl trinitrate.

items.t: Never take sildenafil, tadalafil or vardenafil (erectile dysfunction medicines) with this medicine.

src.q: Glyceryl trinitrate is contraindicated in patients taking phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil)

items.t: A fresh tablet should give a slight burning feeling under the tongue; if not, get a new supply. Carry tablets in a bag or wallet, not close to the body.

src.q: A fresh tablet should produce a slight burning sensation when placed under the tongue; if this does not occur, obtain a fresh supply
If you need to carry them with you DO NOT carry them close to your body, rather in a purse, wallet or handbag.

items.t: Dizziness can occur; check you are not affected before driving. Alcohol makes this worse.

src.q: As Glyceryl trinitrate can cause dizziness, patients should make sure they are not affected before driving or operating machinery. This effect appears to be accentuated by alcohol.
